scope: Static review of one normal Android AMS numeric-PID compaction request. No reviewer phone execution. Does not establish action completion or available-memory gain.
verified: Skip action when current available RAM already meets the unchanged4026531840-byte firstboot floor.
Skip action when current free swap is below20percent of total swap; Android retained low-swap behavior is not overridden.
Root, canonical receipt base, exact process start time, stable UID/kernel OOM priority, uniquely recorded frozen cached-empty AMS state and no pending freeze are checked.
Final process snapshot is rechecked after the last potentially slow AMS observation, then RAM and free swap are sampled immediately before receipt reservation.
Exclusive JSONL receipt reserves one request; no repeated action loop or overwrite path.
Only requested mutation is /system/bin/am compact full for the checked numeric PID; no process termination, manual thaw, cache drop or global setting change.
Subprocess timeouts are15seconds and observation delay3seconds; resulting state and command status are recorded.
Reported compaction-record advancement requires both timestamps to be actual integers and a strict increase; unchanged PID/start/UID/OOM and frozen cached-empty state are reported separately.
limits: A check and a later asynchronous AMS request cannot make process/resource state atomic; the implementation uses immediate rechecks and Android existing mechanism.
System-wide MemAvailable differences can include unrelated memory changes.
Raw private app/process inventory is not included in this review.
